complexity_rationale: Concurrent reservation under SELECT FOR UPDATE row locks with the no-negative invariant, dual sync-HTTP + async-event paths, in-process expiry sweeper using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, outbox publisher for events.reservation.expired, five state-driven event consumers (payment.completed/failed/expired, order.cancelled, product.created), and a documented multi-SKU lock-order pin (ADR-005). State-driven consumer rule (ADR-009) is load-bearing for the PR-003 cross-topic race resolution.

scaffold.common_lib_import: B2C E-Commerce Platform/backend/common (wrapper, middleware, token, database, kafka, validator)

directory_layout.cmd/inventory/main.go: Service entrypoint; wires DI; loads INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET (≥32 bytes) and validates length; starts HTTP server, Kafka consumers, sweeper goroutine, outbox-relay goroutine.
directory_layout.router/router.go: Registers POST /api/v1/inventory/* routes per cross-cutting.route-convention. Public health under GET /liveness, /readiness, /metrics. Internal-secret-only routes use common/middleware/internal_auth (constant-time compare per ADR-008); admin route uses common/middleware/jwt with role==ADMIN.
directory_layout.config/config.go: Env-driven config; binds RESERVATION_TTL_MINUTES (default 15, source-of-truth = cross-cutting.pricing.constants), SWEEPER_CADENCE_SECONDS (default 30), SWEEPER_BATCH_SIZE (default 200), OUTBOX_RELAY_CADENCE_SECONDS (default 5), MIGRATIONS_AUTO_APPLY (dev only). Refuses to boot if INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET is unset or <32 bytes.
directory_layout.app/stock/: stock_levels read paths + admin adjust handler.
directory_layout.app/reservation/: reservation create handler + reservation release handler + internal commit/release functions + sweeper goroutine.
directory_layout.app/outbox/: outbox row writer (used inside business txs) + relayer goroutine (publishes to Kafka).
directory_layout.app/access/: pgx repositories for stock_levels, reservations, stock_adjustments, outbox_events, consumed_events, idempotency_keys.
directory_layout.migrations/: SQL files applied at boot when MIGRATIONS_AUTO_APPLY=true (local/dev only).

tables.name: stock_levels

columns.name: version
columns.purpose: OPTLOCK defensive check; SELECT FOR UPDATE row lock is the binding mechanism per cross-cutting.persistence.concurrency

tables.notes: INV-008 no-negative invariant is enforced at three layers (tx-level guard, CHECK constraint, optimistic version).

tables.name: reservations
indexes: PARTIAL INDEX idx_reservations_sweeper (status, expires_at) WHERE status = 'RESERVED'   -- drives sweeper SCAN cheaply
notes: (order_id) is the natural lookup key for state-driven event consumers; one orderId may have multiple rows (one per SKU). Lookup uses idx_reservations_order_id and re-locks every row FOR UPDATE inside the consumer tx.
EXPIRED is written by the sweeper (release_reason='EXPIRED'). RELEASED is written by event-driven release paths and the HTTP release endpoint.
COMMITTED rows that are later released via PR-006 admin-cancel-of-PAID transition COMMITTED→RELEASED with release_reason='PAID_SOFT_CANCEL' to make audit grepping easy.

tables.name: stock_adjustments
tables.notes: INV-007 admin audit row; written in the same tx as the stock_levels mutation.

tables.name: outbox_events
indexes: PARTIAL INDEX idx_outbox_unpublished (id) WHERE published_at IS NULL
tables.notes: Per cross-cutting.persistence.outbox_pattern + ADR-004. Single-threaded relayer goroutine polls every 5s, ORDER BY id ASC, LIMIT 100; publishes via common/kafka with key=aggregate_id (orderId); marks published_at on success. At-least-once delivery — consumers dedup on payload.eventId.

tables.name: consumed_events
tables.notes: Per-service consumer dedup table. INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING inside the same tx that applies the event side-effect; zero rows-affected on the dedup INSERT means duplicate — early-return idempotent no-op.

tables.name: idempotency_keys
tables.notes: Server-side idempotency-key store. FOR UPDATE on this row serializes concurrent same-key callers; second waiter takes the replay branch.

CREATE TABLE reservations + FK(sku) + idx_reservations_order_id + partial idx_reservations_sweeper.
CREATE TABLE consumed_events with composite PK.

concurrency_model.lock_ordering_pin: ALWAYS lock stock_levels(sku) FIRST, THEN reservations(id) inside any state-mutating tx. Within a single multi-SKU reservation.create call, lock SKUs in lexicographic order (ORDER BY sku ASC) before any reservation INSERT. This is the single canonical lock-order pin (per ADR-005) — preventing deadlocks under concurrent multi-SKU checkouts.
concurrency_model.row_lock_primitive: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on stock_levels(sku) and reservations(id). The sweeper's candidate-scan additionally uses FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED to allow horizontal-replica scaling without contention on the same expired row.
no_negative_invariant_layers: Layer 1 (tx-level guard): handler computes (current.available_qty - requested) under the FOR UPDATE row lock; if negative, ROLLBACK and return 409.
Layer 2 (Postgres CHECK constraint): CHECK (available_qty >= 0) on stock_levels — defense in depth; fires STOCK_NEGATIVE_INVARIANT (mapped from PG error 23514) if any path slips past Layer 1.
Layer 3 (optimistic version): stock_levels.version is incremented on every mutating UPDATE; mismatch is panic-class log + 500 (should be unreachable since FOR UPDATE serializes writers).
concurrency_model.expected_hot_rows: Top-selling SKUs (flash-sale items). Mitigation if needed: shard hot SKUs across multiple stock_levels rows (deferred to v2).

endpoints.auth_notes: ADMIN-only. CUSTOMER token → 403 AUTH_FORBIDDEN per cross-cutting.auth.role_rejection_rules. Public-internet-reachable through gateway (admin uses curl/Postman per BA out_of_scope on admin UI).

error_contract.trigger: delta=0, reason missing/empty/too-long, or sku invalid

edge_behavior.idempotency: Optional client-supplied Idempotency-Key honored per cross-cutting.idempotency (scope per-(endpoint, actorUserId)). Replay returns persisted envelope verbatim. Same key + different request_hash → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.
side_effects: UPDATE stock_levels SET available_qty = available_qty + delta, version = version + 1, updated_at = NOW()
INSERT stock_adjustments (id, sku, delta, reason, actor_user_id) — same tx
edge_behavior.transactionality: Single Postgres tx: SELECT FOR UPDATE → guard → UPDATE → INSERT audit row → COMMIT

behavior_pseudocode: BEGIN TX
validate(delta != 0, len(reason) in [1,255]) → VALIDATION_ERROR
row = SELECT * FROM stock_levels WHERE sku = $1 FOR UPDATE
if row is null → ROLLBACK; NOT_FOUND
if row.available_qty + delta < 0 → ROLLBACK; STOCK_NEGATIVE_INVARIANT
UPDATE stock_levels SET available_qty = available_qty + delta, version = version + 1, updated_at = NOW() WHERE sku = $1
adjustmentId = uuidv7()
INSERT INTO stock_adjustments (id, sku, delta, reason, actor_user_id) VALUES (adjustmentId, $1, delta, reason, claims.sub)
if Idempotency-Key header present: persist response_envelope into idempotency_keys atomically
COMMIT
return SUCCESS {sku, availableQty: row.available_qty + delta, adjustmentId}
implementation_hints: Map PG error 23514 (CHECK violation) → STOCK_NEGATIVE_INVARIANT (defensive; layer-1 guard should reject first)

endpoints.name: reservation.create
endpoints.auth_notes: Called by Checkout (step 6 of checkout.commit) over the private network plane with X-Internal-Secret + Idempotency-Key=newOrderId per cross-cutting.idempotency.internal_orderId_rule.

reservationId.description: First-row id (deterministic by ORDER BY sku ASC); informational/audit only — all consumer/release lookups are by orderId.

validation_rules: orderId is UUID v7; items non-empty (1..50); every qty>=1

error_contract.trigger: empty items, qty<=0, idempotencyKey != orderId, or expiresAt malformed
any item.qty > stock.available_qty (response carries per-item details: [{sku, requestedQty, availableQty}])
defensive — concurrent racer slipped past FOR UPDATE; CHECK constraint fires

edge_behavior.idempotency: Server-side keyed on (key=orderId, endpoint='inventory.reservation.create'). First-call persists envelope inside the same tx as the business writes. Replay (same key + same request_hash) returns persisted envelope verbatim. Same key + different request_hash → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. Concurrent same-key callers serialize via FOR UPDATE on idempotency_keys; second waiter takes the replay branch.
side_effects: INSERT idempotency_keys (key=orderId, endpoint, request_hash, response_envelope, http_status, expires_at = NOW() + 24h)
UPDATE stock_levels SET available_qty -= qty, reserved_qty += qty, version += 1 — once per item (in lex sku order)
INSERT reservations (id, order_id, sku, qty, status='RESERVED', expires_at) — once per item
edge_behavior.transactionality: Single Postgres tx covering: idempotency check → multi-SKU FOR UPDATE (lex sku order — ADR-005) → per-SKU validate → per-SKU UPDATE stock + INSERT reservation → idempotency_keys persist → COMMIT.
edge_behavior.lock_order: stock_levels(sku) FIRST in lex sku order, THEN reservations(id) inserts. Single canonical pin — see ADR-005.

behavior_pseudocode: validate(orderId UUID, items non-empty, every qty>=1, idempotencyKey == orderId, expiresAt is RFC3339) → VALIDATION_ERROR
request_hash = sha256(canonical_json({orderId, items[sorted by sku]}))
BEGIN TX
-- IDEMPOTENCY (cross-cutting.idempotency.behavior)
existing = SELECT * FROM idempotency_keys WHERE key=orderId AND endpoint='inventory.reservation.create' FOR UPDATE
if existing AND existing.request_hash == request_hash → COMMIT; return existing.response_envelope (replay)
if existing AND existing.request_hash != request_hash → ROLLBACK; return 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED
-- LOCK ORDER PIN (ADR-005): stock_levels first, in ascending sku order, BEFORE any reservation insert
sortedSkus = sort_unique(items[].sku)
stockRows = SELECT sku, available_qty, reserved_qty, version FROM stock_levels WHERE sku = ANY(sortedSkus) ORDER BY sku ASC FOR UPDATE
-- per-SKU validation
insufficientList = []
for each item in items:
row = stockRows[item.sku]
if row is null → insufficientList += {sku: item.sku, requestedQty: item.qty, availableQty: 0}   -- treat as INSUFFICIENT_STOCK
elif row.available_qty < item.qty → insufficientList += {sku, requestedQty: item.qty, availableQty: row.available_qty}
if insufficientList non-empty → ROLLBACK; return 409 INSUFFICIENT_STOCK with details: insufficientList
-- mutate per sku in deterministic ORDER BY sku ASC; rows are already locked
reservationIds = []
for each item in items (ORDER BY sku ASC):
UPDATE stock_levels SET available_qty = available_qty - item.qty, reserved_qty = reserved_qty + item.qty, version = version + 1, updated_at = NOW() WHERE sku = item.sku
rid = uuidv7()
INSERT INTO reservations (id, order_id, sku, qty, status, expires_at) VALUES (rid, orderId, item.sku, item.qty, 'RESERVED', expiresAt)
reservationIds += rid
responseData = {reservationId: reservationIds[0], items: items.map(reserved=true), expiresAt}
envelope = {code: 'SUCCESS', message: 'reserved', data: responseData, traceId}
INSERT INTO idempotency_keys (key=orderId, endpoint='inventory.reservation.create', request_hash, response_envelope=envelope, http_status=200, expires_at=NOW()+24h)
COMMIT
return envelope
implementation_hints: common/validator binding tags for nested struct validation
Map PG error 23505 (unique violation) on idempotency_keys → race-with-self (FOR UPDATE should prevent; defensive)
Use sort.Slice on items by sku BEFORE the SELECT FOR UPDATE — sorting at the application level keeps the SQL simple

endpoints.name: reservation.release
endpoints.auth_notes: Called by Checkout as compensation on post-step-6 failure of checkout.commit per cross-cutting.persistence.transactional_boundaries (ADR-007). NOT used by event consumers — they call ReservationService.Release directly to avoid loopback overhead.

reservationId.description: Optional; informational. Lookup is by orderId — one orderId may have multiple reservation rows.

validation_rules: orderId is UUID; reason in enum

error_contract.trigger: orderId malformed or reason not in enum

edge_behavior.idempotency: Idempotent on order_id (per-row idempotent on reservations.id). Re-invocation on already-RELEASED/EXPIRED rows is a no-op. COMMITTED rows transition sold→available with release_reason='PAID_SOFT_CANCEL' (BA PR-006 MVP policy).
side_effects: UPDATE stock_levels per sku (available_qty += qty; reserved_qty -= qty OR sold_qty -= qty depending on prior state)
UPDATE reservations SET status='RELEASED', released_at=NOW(), release_reason=<reason or 'PAID_SOFT_CANCEL'>
edge_behavior.transactionality: Single Postgres tx covering: SELECT reservations FOR UPDATE ORDER BY sku ASC → per-row state-driven branch → COMMIT.
edge_behavior.lock_order: stock_levels(sku) BEFORE reservations(id); reservations rows iterated ORDER BY sku ASC.

behavior_pseudocode: validate(orderId UUID, reason in {PAYMENT_FAILED, PAYMENT_EXPIRED, ORDER_CANCELLED, ADMIN_FORCE}) → VALIDATION_ERROR
BEGIN TX
rows = SELECT * FROM reservations WHERE order_id = $1 ORDER BY sku ASC FOR UPDATE
if rows is empty → ROLLBACK; RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND
for each r in rows:
if r.status == 'RELEASED' or r.status == 'EXPIRED' → continue (idempotent no-op)
if r.status == 'RESERVED':
stock = SELECT * FROM stock_levels WHERE sku = r.sku FOR UPDATE
UPDATE stock_levels SET available_qty = available_qty + r.qty, reserved_qty = reserved_qty - r.qty, version = version + 1 WHERE sku = r.sku
UPDATE reservations SET status = 'RELEASED', released_at = NOW(), release_reason = $reason WHERE id = r.id
if r.status == 'COMMITTED':   -- PR-006 soft-cancel-of-PAID branch (also reachable via order.cancelled consumer)
stock = SELECT * FROM stock_levels WHERE sku = r.sku FOR UPDATE
UPDATE stock_levels SET sold_qty = sold_qty - r.qty, available_qty = available_qty + r.qty, version = version + 1 WHERE sku = r.sku
UPDATE reservations SET status = 'RELEASED', released_at = NOW(), release_reason = 'PAID_SOFT_CANCEL' WHERE id = r.id
COMMIT
return SUCCESS {reservationId: rows[0].id, status: 'RELEASED'}
implementation_hints: Reuse internal ReservationService.Release for both the HTTP path and the event-consumer path — keeps state-driven branching in one function
callers: checkout (compensation on post-step-6 failure of checkout.commit per cross-cutting.persistence.transactional_boundaries / ADR-007)

system_internal_jobs.name: reservation.sweep-expired
system_internal_jobs.type: SYSTEM_INTERNAL (NO HTTP route, NO JWT, NO caller)
system_internal_jobs.trigger: in-process scheduler (time.Ticker) inside the inventory service, started at boot from cmd/inventory/main.go

SWEEPER_CADENCE_SECONDS.purpose: ticker fire interval; named in code as reservation.sweepCadence

SWEEPER_BATCH_SIZE.purpose: per-tick LIMIT; named in code as reservation.sweepBatchSize

RESERVATION_TTL_MINUTES.purpose: TTL anchor; sweeper reads expires_at directly; constant referenced by reservation.create stays in lockstep

algorithm_pseudocode: // runs in a single goroutine; ticker fires every SWEEPER_CADENCE_SECONDS
// horizontal scaling: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on the candidate scan ensures replicas pick disjoint sets
// ── PHASE 1: pick candidates (short tx; SKIP LOCKED for replica safety) ─────────
candidates = SELECT id, order_id, sku, qty FROM reservations
COMMIT TX_scan   -- releases scan locks; per-row tx below re-locks individually
-- canonical lock-order pin: stock_levels FIRST, then reservations (ADR-005)
stock = SELECT * FROM stock_levels WHERE sku = c.sku FOR UPDATE
r     = SELECT * FROM reservations WHERE id = c.id FOR UPDATE
if r.status != 'RESERVED' → ROLLBACK; continue   -- another path moved the row (commit/release/prior tick)
UPDATE reservations SET status = 'EXPIRED', released_at = NOW(), release_reason = 'EXPIRED' WHERE id = r.id
INSERT INTO outbox_events (id, aggregate_id = r.order_id, event_type = 'reservation.expired',
// periodic gauge sample (every Nth tick) to avoid query-per-tick cost
gauge   reservations_pending_expiry = SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reservations WHERE status='RESERVED' AND expires_at < NOW()
system_internal_jobs.ordering_within_tick: ORDER BY expires_at ASC — older expirations release first.
system_internal_jobs.horizontal_scaling: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on PHASE 1 scan ensures two inventory replicas never contend on the same row. PHASE 2 per-row tx re-locks individually — bounded tx-time, fault-isolated.
failure_modes: DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE — log + skip tick; next tick retries.
Outbox publisher lag — events.reservation.expired publication is decoupled via outbox (ADR-004); consumers (Order) absorb at-least-once delivery + dedup on eventId.
Crash mid-batch — partial rows are committed per-row (PHASE 2 is per-row tx); remaining candidates re-scanned next tick (their FOR UPDATE locks evaporated with the rolled-back tx).
observability: log structured fields: tick_started_at, candidate_count, released_count, errored_count, tick_duration_ms

event_consumers.idempotency_strategy: Two-layer dedup: (1) consumed_events INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING — zero rows-affected → already processed, ack and return; (2) state-driven SELECT reservations FOR UPDATE — branch on CURRENT row state per ADR-009, ignore event.fromStatus.
behavior_pseudocode: BEGIN TX
// LAYER 1: consumed_events dedup
rowsAffected = INSERT INTO consumed_events (event_id, consumer_name) VALUES ($eventId, 'inventory.payment-completed') ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
if rowsAffected == 0 → COMMIT; ack (idempotent replay)
// LAYER 2: state-driven (ADR-009) — read current state, ignore implicit fromStatus
rows = SELECT * FROM reservations WHERE order_id = $orderId ORDER BY sku ASC FOR UPDATE
for each r in rows:
branch on CURRENT r.status:
RESERVED  →
stock = SELECT * FROM stock_levels WHERE sku = r.sku FOR UPDATE
UPDATE stock_levels SET reserved_qty -= r.qty, sold_qty += r.qty, version += 1 WHERE sku = r.sku
UPDATE reservations SET status = 'COMMITTED' WHERE id = r.id
COMMITTED →
no-op (idempotent re-delivery)
RELEASED  →
log warn 'payment.completed arrived after reservation released for orderId={}' (PR-003 race)
counter inventory_reservation_conflict_total += 1
no mutation
EXPIRED   →
same as RELEASED (sweeper got there first)
COMMIT (ack on success only; transient failure → at-least-once redelivery)

event_consumers.idempotency_strategy: Two-layer: consumed_events PK + state-driven SELECT FOR UPDATE.
behavior_pseudocode: BEGIN TX
if INSERT consumed_events ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING returns 0 rows → ack and return
rows = SELECT * FROM reservations WHERE order_id = $orderId ORDER BY sku ASC FOR UPDATE
for each r in rows:
RESERVED  →
stock = SELECT * FROM stock_levels WHERE sku = r.sku FOR UPDATE
UPDATE stock_levels SET available_qty += r.qty, reserved_qty -= r.qty, version += 1 WHERE sku = r.sku
UPDATE reservations SET status='RELEASED', released_at=NOW(), release_reason='PAYMENT_FAILED' WHERE id = r.id
COMMITTED → defensive log 'payment.failed arrived for COMMITTED reservation (should be unreachable due to PAYMENT_INTENT_TERMINAL guard)'; no-op
RELEASED → no-op (idempotent)
EXPIRED  → no-op (sweeper got there first)
COMMIT

event_consumers.idempotency_strategy: Two-layer: consumed_events PK + state-driven SELECT FOR UPDATE.
behavior_pseudocode: // Identical to payment.failed for inventory's purposes (per contract)
BEGIN TX
if dedup-insert returns 0 rows → ack and return
rows = SELECT * FROM reservations WHERE order_id = $orderId ORDER BY sku ASC FOR UPDATE
for each r in rows:
RESERVED  → release; release_reason = 'PAYMENT_EXPIRED'
COMMITTED → defensive log; no-op
RELEASED  → no-op
EXPIRED   → no-op (the sweeper-driven path that often DROVE this event in the first place; idempotent)
COMMIT

event_consumers.idempotency_strategy: Two-layer: consumed_events PK + state-driven SELECT FOR UPDATE. CANONICAL state-driven branch per ADR-009 + contracts.json:events.order.cancelled.failure_modes (PR-003 + PR-006). MUST NOT branch on event.fromStatus.
behavior_pseudocode: // CANONICAL state-driven (ADR-009) — IGNORE event.fromStatus; read current row state
BEGIN TX
if dedup-insert returns 0 rows → ack and return
rows = SELECT * FROM reservations WHERE order_id = $orderId ORDER BY sku ASC FOR UPDATE
for each r in rows:
RESERVED  →
stock = SELECT * FROM stock_levels WHERE sku = r.sku FOR UPDATE
UPDATE stock_levels SET available_qty += r.qty, reserved_qty -= r.qty, version += 1 WHERE sku = r.sku
UPDATE reservations SET status='RELEASED', released_at=NOW(), release_reason='ORDER_CANCELLED' WHERE id = r.id
// typical PENDING_PAYMENT customer-cancel path
COMMITTED →
stock = SELECT * FROM stock_levels WHERE sku = r.sku FOR UPDATE
UPDATE stock_levels SET sold_qty -= r.qty, available_qty += r.qty, version += 1 WHERE sku = r.sku
UPDATE reservations SET status='RELEASED', released_at=NOW(), release_reason='PAID_SOFT_CANCEL' WHERE id = r.id
// covers (a) admin-cancel of PAID order per BA PR-006 MVP policy AND (b) PR-003 race where payment.completed was consumed before order.cancelled
RELEASED  → no-op (already released by sweeper, prior cancellation, or prior payment.failed/expired)
EXPIRED   → no-op
COMMIT
event_consumers.notes: MUST NEVER read event.fromStatus to decide its branch. event.fromStatus is informational/audit only per ADR-009.

event_consumers.idempotency_strategy: Two-layer: consumed_events PK + natural idempotency via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (sku) DO NOTHING (no state-mutation conflict possible).
behavior_pseudocode: BEGIN TX
if INSERT consumed_events ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING returns 0 rows → ack and return
INSERT INTO stock_levels (sku, available_qty, reserved_qty, sold_qty, version)
VALUES ($sku, 0, 0, 0, 0)
ON CONFLICT (sku) DO NOTHING
COMMIT
event_consumers.notes: Initial qty seeded to 0 per TL contract (payload carries no initial_qty); admin uses inventory.stock.adjust to set initial inventory. Until inventory has seeded the SKU, listing with inStock=true filters this product out (per catalog contract).

event_producers.emit_path: outbox_events table → in-process relayer goroutine → Kafka via common/kafka

relayer.query: SELECT id, aggregate_id, event_type, payload_json FROM outbox_events WHERE published_at IS NULL ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT 100
relayer.publish_then_mark: for each row: producer.Send(topic='ecom.inventory.events', key=aggregate_id, value=payload_json) → on success UPDATE outbox_events SET published_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1
relayer.delivery_semantics: at-least-once (per ADR-004); consumers dedup on payload.eventId
relayer.panic_recovery: outer recover() per tick; one bad row never kills the loop

event_producers.produced_by: inventory.reservation.sweep-expired (writes outbox row in same tx as the EXPIRED transition)

td_ambiguity_notes.tl_contract_says: callers: 'inventory's own payment.completed consumer (primary). HTTP path retained for ops tooling.'
td_ambiguity_notes.td_decision: DROP the HTTP route in MVP. Reservation commit is implemented as INTERNAL_FUNCTION (ReservationService.Commit) called only from the events.payment.completed consumer. Rationale: (a) no production caller exists; (b) per the user's TD instruction the inventory HTTP surface is 'stock.read, stock.bulk-read, stock.adjust, reservation.create, reservation.release' — commit is intentionally not exposed; (c) cross-cutting.route-convention.examples.inventory still LISTS POST /reservation/commit, so this is a TD-level deviation flagged for Plan-Reviewer. Ops tooling, if needed later, can be added as an admin-scoped endpoint.
td_ambiguity_notes.owner_to_decide: Plan-Reviewer (TD elects 'do not expose'; surface flagged ready to flip if reviewer disagrees)

td_ambiguity_notes.tl_contract_says: cross-cutting.persistence.transactional_boundaries: 'On any sync-call failure, checkout calls inventory.reservation.release as compensation' AND connectivity.md auth-boundaries table lists '/api/v1/inventory/reservation/create|commit|release' under X-Internal-Secret.
td_ambiguity_notes.td_decision: internal_secret (X-Internal-Secret with constant-time compare). Aligns with connectivity.md and the user's instruction ('Internal HTTP: reservation.create ... reservation.release (compensation)'). The earlier td.json variant suggesting CUSTOMER-JWT for customer-cancel is INCORRECT — customer-cancel flows from the user via order.cancel-mine; Inventory then handles the release via the events.order.cancelled consumer, not via a customer-facing HTTP call.

td_ambiguity_notes.tl_contract_says: payload only carries {productId, sku} — no initial_qty.
td_ambiguity_notes.td_decision: Seed stock_levels with zeros (available=0, reserved=0, sold=0). Admin uses inventory.stock.adjust to set initial inventory. Consumer uses ON CONFLICT (sku) DO NOTHING for natural idempotency. Until a positive delta lands via stock.adjust, catalog's inStock filter omits the product.

td_ambiguity_notes.topic: reservationId returned by reservation.create (one row per SKU vs. one group id)
td_ambiguity_notes.tl_contract_says: response_data.reservationId is singular but reservation table is one row per SKU.
td_ambiguity_notes.td_decision: Return reservationIds[0] (the first inserted row's UUID v7, deterministic by ORDER BY sku ASC). All reservation lookups in event consumers / release / commit are by order_id (NOT reservationId), so the returned id is informational/audit-only. If TL prefers a separate group-id column, schema change is local to inventory.

td_ambiguity_notes.tl_contract_says: cross-cutting.idempotency.failure_modes lists IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INFLIGHT for concurrent same-key calls.
td_ambiguity_notes.td_decision: Use Postgres FOR UPDATE on idempotency_keys to serialize concurrent same-key calls (waiter blocks until the first commit then takes the replay branch). Do NOT return IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INFLIGHT under default config — Checkout will rarely double-fire with the same orderId. Reserve the code for a future config-tunable lock-timeout.
